clue.text: Indian state corporation skirting conflict area

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the belly word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a gut
a jar is a quarrel or clash

explanation.surface: A big company is said to be avoiding a war zone somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but here it is the old humorous word for a large stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarat is a state on the west coast of India, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Lord adopting a kid displays greatness

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the exclamation word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Lord!' are both exclamations of surprise
to kid is to tease or joke, a jest

explanation.surface: A nobleman taking in a young goat shows his grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' is not a peer but an exclamation, swapped for its fellow exclamation MY; 'kid' is joking, not a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is regal grandeur or stateliness, a close synonym for greatness.

clue.text: Report from aircraft of point on missile containing rings

parts.note: S is a compass point, south

indicators.note: the missile abbreviation holds the ring letters within it

parts.note: ICBM is an intercontinental ballistic missile
O looks like a ring, so two rings are OO

explanation.surface: A news report from a plane about a point on a missile with rings round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a written account, but here it is a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A supersonic aircraft makes an explosive bang, a report in the sense of a loud noise.

clue.text: Resort for us clubbers primarily?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, an instruction to sort the letters again into a new order
primarily picks the first letter of each of the words us and clubbers

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where young night-clubbers like us go first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' does double duty in the reading: as a holiday resort it is the definition, as 're-sort' it rearranges FOR with U and C, the first letters of 'us' and 'clubbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island famous as a party holiday destination for young clubbers.

clue.text: Game superb move from back clinches

indicators.note: reading from the back means the run of letters is taken right to left
to clinch is to hold tightly, so the two words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: In some game, a superb move backwards seals the win.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ERBMO sit across 'superb move' and read backwards give the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old three-handed card game popular in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Source of amusement nightly, parking a convertible

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A convertible car parked each night is somebody's toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' suggests a soft-top car beside 'parking', but it signals the anagram of NIGHTLY, P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaything is a toy, something used purely for amusement.

clue.text: Never setting off with the reader's biography

parts.note: a switch that is off is not on
the reader of the clue is you, so the reader's is yours
a biography is a life story, a life

explanation.surface: Something is being set off alongside a biography of whoever is reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' just places the parts side by side, and 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, an idiomatic way of saying certainly not, never.

clue.text: Lie by one's bed after greeting Henry's famous words?

indicators.note: the lie, one's and bed pieces come after the greeting

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
a story is a fib, a lie
one's reads as one is, I'S, giving IS
a bunk is a narrow bed

explanation.surface: Someone lies on their bed after saying hello, quoting Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford said history is more or less bunk; the clue's 'Lie' and 'bed' pull towards sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation is Henry Ford's famous dismissal of the past, from a 1916 newspaper interview.

clue.text: Tease lieutenant keeping a long way back in battle

indicators.note: back turns the whole run of pieces round to read right to left

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the officer abbreviation holds the next pieces

parts.note: far means a long way off

explanation.surface: Someone teases a lieutenant who stays well behind during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses everything: RAG + LT holding AFAR makes RAGLAFART, which read backwards is the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar was the naval battle of 1805 in which Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: Potential instigator of post war rumble with time

parts.note: a roll is a long rumble, as of thunder or drums

explanation.surface: Something that might start trouble after a war rumbles on over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post war' reads as after a war, but means a flame war started by an online post.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet troll posts provocative messages to start arguments, often called flame wars.

clue.text: At entering stag party, is unable to stand

indicators.note: the first word goes into the party word

parts.note: a stag party is men only, all of them he's

explanation.surface: At a stag do, someone can't bear it.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is male only, so it is a gathering of HE'S, the plural of he.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unable to stand something is to detest it, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Open-air cafe, note, medium for culture and study

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
agar is the jelly on which bacterial cultures are grown
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: An outdoor cafe noted as a place of culture and learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Culture' suggests the arts, but here it is a lab culture grown on a medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor place where refreshments are served, an open-air cafe.

clue.text: Factory and post office moving to West Midlands town

parts.note: a works is a factory

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A factory and a post office relocate to a town in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Midlands' looks like the region, but 'West' belongs with 'moving to'; Worksop is in Nottinghamshire, in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town in north Nottinghamshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Paddy's brown suit specially chosen without a second thought?

definitions.note: Paddy's reads as paddy is, the 's being the link

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: the second-thought letters are taken away from the suit word

parts.note: trumps is the card suit chosen to rank above the others
PS, a postscript, is a thought added afterwards

explanation.surface: An Irishman's brown suit was picked on impulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman, but a paddy is a fit of temper in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of bad temper, the same as a tantrum.

clue.text: Frenchman singing at last when accompanied by fiddle

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of singing

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
a con is a swindle, a fiddle

explanation.surface: A Frenchman finally sings while someone plays the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a violin to go with singing, but it means a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gascon is a native of Gascony in south-west France, so a Frenchman.

clue.text: Agent stops eastern vessels: they're a high security risk

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the agent fills the vessels word

parts.note: junks are Chinese sailing ships
James Bond is the famous secret agent

explanation.surface: A spy halts some ships from the east which pose a big security danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'security risk' suggests spies, but securities here are financial: junk bonds carry a high risk of default.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk bonds are high-yield securities with a large risk of default, a pun on security.

clue.text: Most productive taxmen no longer upset Treasury

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the letters upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: IR, the Inland Revenue, was the UK tax office until it merged into HMRC in 2005
a chest is a coffer holding funds, a treasury

explanation.surface: Former taxmen are unhappy with the Treasury about who is most productive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distress, but it turns IR into RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Richest can mean most fertile or productive, as in the richest soil.

clue.text: Common where a pony went galloping

indicators.note: a galloping pony is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A village green where a pony went galloping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like a village green, but means ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Two a penny is a British idiom for very common, plentiful and so of little value.

clue.text: Old lady doctor, a deliverer of poisonous injection?

parts.note: ma is mother, informally the old lady
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A mother who is a doctor gives out a poison jab.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a medic, but it is a snake's bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamba is a highly venomous African snake, whose bite injects poison.

clue.text: Raise pitch rating?

parts.note: to jack up is to raise
pitch is tar, a black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A request to raise a score for the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' and 'rating' suggest music or sport, but a rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is an old name for a sailor, and a rating is a naval sailor without a commission.

clue.text: Caravan site in Kent, perhaps, right by main road

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, SE
the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI

explanation.surface: A caravan park in Kent next to the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caravan site' suggests a British holiday park, but it is a desert travellers' inn; the A1 is a major British road.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai, short for caravanserai, is an inn where desert camel caravans stop.

clue.text: Lovers of money wrongfully acquired with gun

indicators.note: wrongfully means by wrong means, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Lovers of cash got hold of it illegally with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovers of money' reads as a phrase, but 'Lovers' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Young men can mean boyfriends or suitors, as in her young man, so lovers.

clue.text: Being a spotter of talent, he passed on help

parts.note: ob. abbreviates Latin obiit, he died
a help is a domestic servant

explanation.surface: A talent scout passed on help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' suggests declined, but means died.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice, being someone who spots things.

clue.text: Writer's well in — and more familiar — with Kurdish extremists

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: an older friend is one known longer, more familiar

explanation.surface: A writer is in with Kurdish extremists and getting closer to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kurdish extremists' are just K and H, the end letters of 'Kurdish'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkholder is an inkwell, the well a writer dips a pen into.

clue.text: TV programme about Top Gear on the way

parts.note: C, circa, means about
hats are gear worn on top
how is the way something is done

explanation.surface: A TV show about Top Gear, the motoring show, on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Gear' is a British TV motoring show, but here it is headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a TV programme in which a host interviews guests.

clue.text: Famous Greek does donkey derby, maybe, but is coming last

indicators.note: the word is is placed at the end

parts.note: riding in a donkey derby, a seaside donkey race, one is on an ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous Greek enters a donkey race but finishes last.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristotle Onassis was a Greek shipping magnate; a donkey derby is a British fun-day donkey race.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle Onassis was a celebrated Greek shipping tycoon, so a famous Greek.

clue.text: Puritan not normally one bound for King's Cross?

indicators.note: not in the normal way, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A Puritan who is unusually bound for King's Cross station.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an up train is one travelling towards London; King's Cross is a London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: An up train runs towards London, so one heading for King's Cross station is an example.

clue.text: Meeting sometimes accused professor without measure

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the professor surrounds the measure

parts.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo
an en is a printer's unit of measure

explanation.surface: Sometimes a professor is accused of being without measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Cluedo (Clue in North America) is a murder-mystery board game whose suspects include Professor Plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a meeting of all members of a body, a full assembly.

clue.text: American socialite, corrupt, it arises

indicators.note: in a down answer, arising means rising, read bottom to top

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
it is sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: An American socialite is corrupt, it emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' means sex appeal, abbreviated SA; ROTSA reversed gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor was an American-born socialite who became Britain's first sitting woman MP.

clue.text: Turn more powerful gear

definitions.meaning: as wind may rise, increasing in force

explanation.definitionFit: A wind gets up when it strengthens, and a get-up is an outfit or costume, gear.
